sections.h2: Contacting the Graham County Register of Deeds
sections.html:
The office is at 12 North Main Street, Robbinsville, NC 28771. Mail goes to PO Box 406, Robbinsville, NC 28771. The phone is (828) 479-7971 and the fax is (828) 479-6902.

The counter is staffed weekdays, 8:00 to 4:30, with a break at noon. Browsing records needs no appointment. The office may run flex hours or close some days for unforeseen reasons, and on those days recordings are accepted in the Tax Office. Phone ahead if your closing depends on a counter visit.

Fees are payable by cash or check and nothing else. The Tax Office and the assessor work from 196 Knight Street in Robbinsville, and the assessor's phone is (828) 479-7963. A single trip can handle the deed and any tax questions that surface.

The office records legal documents, deeds, plats and certified documents. It also handles notary oaths, marriages, births and deaths. Records are kept under the North Carolina General Statutes and are open to the public.

For a house sale, the items that matter are your vesting deed, any deed of trust and the plat for your lot. Ask whether a plat for your parcel is on file before you list. A missing or dated boundary description can slow a closing.

The county is divided into three townships, Cheoah, Stecoah and Yellow Creek, and carries municipal codes for Robbinsville, Fontana and Santeetlah. Your deed and tax bill may refer to one of these.

Graham publishes a fee sheet of its own, citing G.S. 161, and its real estate lines track the state schedule.

Graham County fee sheet, real estate lines

That sheet carries an October 1, 2011 date, and the deed of trust tier was amended October 1, 2016. A quick call to the office will tell you whether the numbers changed before you write a check.

The state's conveyance tax shows on Graham's sheet as $2 per thousand of price, the same rate as one dollar per $500 in G.S. 105-228.30.

As the seller you hand it over at the counter right before the deed goes on record. County and state split the receipts. Look for it as a separate line on your settlement statement, and ask your closing attorney how it will read on the deed.

sections.h2: Property tax due dates and penalties
sections.html:
Tax notices mail on July 1 with a September 1 due date. Nothing accrues until after January 5.

  • Interest of 2% begins January 6, then 0.75% a month until paid.
  • A second real estate notice goes out each February.
  • Delinquent taxes are published in the Graham Star every April, and advertising fees are added to each listed bill.
  • Enforced collection can start any time after January 5: wage garnishment, bank attachment, a state debt setoff against income tax returns and lottery winnings, levy on rents and foreclosure.

A delinquent bill will not match the printed figure, so ask the collector for the exact payoff first. The tax office has a foreclosure line at (828) 479-7962.

sections.h2: How to pay your Graham County tax bill
sections.html:
Payment works at the counter, over the phone or online. Accepted forms are cash, credit card, money order and checks payable to Graham County. After hours, use the locked drop box at the building's side entrance.

The county does not set or collect the card charge. The processor takes 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum. Partial payments and prepayments go through if the parcel or account number is noted on the check. When a lender escrows your taxes, the bill still lands with you, so forward a copy to the servicer. Bounced checks cost $25.00 or 10 percent, whichever is more.

sections.h2: Other items the tax office bills
sections.html:
Land and buildings are only part of what this office handles. It also values the following and takes exclusion applications.

  • Motor vehicles, boats, jet skis and houseboats.
  • Elderly, present-use value, religious and educational exclusions.
  • January listings of personal property and business personal property, improvements, business listing extensions and value appeals.

Motor vehicle tax is a separate bill payable to the NCDMV office at 74 S. Main Street in Robbinsville, phone (828) 479-4896. A houseboat sticker costs $5.00 and requires a copy of the pump out permit when you pay. Own a boat or houseboat? Clear those bills before closing so a buyer does not inherit them.

Elderly, disabled and veteran exclusion forms come from the assessor or the collector. Either way they go back to the assessor by June 1.

Graham has a 2027 Schedule of Values built on market values as of January 1, 2027, and a separate present-use schedule for farm and forest land. Two exclusions matter most for a homeowner. G.S. 105-277.1 removes $25,000 or half of appraised value, whichever is larger, for an owner 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled. G.S. 105-277.1C removes $45,000 for a disabled veteran, with no age or income test. Personal property listing runs January 1 through January 31. Call the assessor at (828) 479-7963 with questions.

sections.h2: What happens if property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax stays attached to the parcel from the listing date onward. G.S. 105-374 lets the county bring a foreclosure action, patterned on mortgage foreclosure, in the county where the property is located.

Notice goes to the owner of record, a spouse and other lienholders. The land is auctioned on the courthouse steps, and the commissioner may demand up to 20 percent down. Anyone wanting to raise the bid or file an exception has 10 days after the sale report. An owner can still redeem before confirmation by paying the taxes plus penalties, interest and costs. Behind on the bill? Phone the collector early, because newspaper advertising fees get added to each listed account.

Pay the tax bill, make sure each old loan has a recorded satisfaction, and let your closing attorney review the chain of title.

Under G.S. 47-18, whichever document is registered first in the land's county generally wins over later ones. Satisfactions cost nothing to record here. Did the deed holder die? Finish the estate paperwork first, since the buyer's lender wants proof of signing authority in the index before it funds.

A workable order: get a written balance from the collector, gather your payoff letters, have the satisfactions recorded, then hand the attorney your vesting deed and any plat. A cash buyer skips a lender's title review, but the recorded chain still has to be clean.

faqs.q: Can I pay Graham County recording fees by card?
faqs.a: No, recording fees take cash or a check only. Cards work for property tax at the tax office, with a processor fee added.

faqs.q: What if the Graham County office is closed when I need to record?
faqs.a: Phone (828) 479-7971 before you go. During flex hours or a closure, the Tax Office takes recordings. Bring cash or a check for the fees.

faqs.q: What are the recording charges in Graham County?
faqs.a: Expect $26 for a land record instrument through page 15 and $64 for a deed of trust through page 35, then $4 per extra page. Satisfactions are free.

faqs.q: When are Graham County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Notices mail July 1, and payment is due September 1. Interest of 2% begins January 6.

faqs.q: Is the Graham County transfer tax the same as the statewide rate?
faqs.a: Yes. The sheet shows $2 per thousand, equal to $1 for each $500 of price, and the seller pays it ahead of recording.
